title: The Authenticity Gap in Human Evaluation
abstract: arXiv:2205.11930v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Human ratings are the gold standard in NLG evaluation. The standard protocol is to collect ratings of generated text, average across annotators, and rank NLG systems by their average scores. However, little consideration has been given as to whether this approach faithfully captures human preferences. Analyzing this standard protocol through the lens of utility theory in economics, we identify the implicit assumptions it makes about annotators. These assumptions are often violated in practice, in which case annotator ratings cease to reflect their preferences. The most egregious violations come from using Likert scales, which provably reverse the direction of the true preference in certain cases. We suggest improvements to the standard protocol to make it more theoretically sound, but even in its improved form, it cannot be used to evaluate open-ended tasks like story generation. translated_title: 人类评估中的真实性差距
translated_abstract: arXiv:2205.11930v3 公告类型：替换-交叉 摘要：人类评分是自然语言生成（NLG）评估中的黄金标准。标准流程是收集生成文本的评分，对标注者进行平均，并根据平均分数对NLG系统进行排名。然而，对于这种方法是否忠实捕捉了人类偏好，却鲜有考量。通过经济学中的效用理论视角分析这一标准流程，我们识别出它对标注者所做的隐含假设。这些假设在实践中常被违背，此时标注者的评分不再反映其真实偏好。最严重的违背来自使用李克特量表，这在某些情况下可证明会颠倒真实偏好的方向。我们建议改进标准流程以使其在理论上更稳健，但即使改进后，它仍无法用于评估像故事生成这样的开放任务。对于后者，我们提出了一种新的人类评估方法。
tldr: 本文通过效用理论揭示标准NLG人类评估流程中的隐含假设缺陷，指出李克特量表可能颠倒真实偏好，并提出改进方案及针对开放任务的新评估方法。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals implicit assumption flaws in standard NLG human evaluation via utility theory, showing Likert scales can reverse true preferences, and proposes improvements plus a new method for open-ended tasks.
